spans.text: Emotion regulation paradigm

description.value: Participants viewed neutral and negative pictures or downregulated their emotional responses to negative pictures using distraction or cognitive reappraisal.

spans.text: we used an event-related design

stimuli.value: negative and neutral pictures from the International Affective Picture System

spans.text: Pictures were selected from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS)
Responses were given on an fMRI-ready keyboard
view neutral
To provide a neutral baseline condition, 10 neutral pictures were additionally presented in the view neutral condition.

description.value: Participants viewed neutral pictures and responded naturally, allowing whatever reaction the picture normally evoked; the condition served as a neutral baseline.

spans.text: In the view negative condition, participants attended to the content of negative pictures and responded naturally, allowing themselves to have whatever reaction the picture would normally evoke in them.
view negative
In the view negative condition, participants attended to the content of negative pictures and responded naturally

description.value: Participants viewed negative pictures and attended to their content while responding naturally, allowing whatever emotional reaction the picture normally evoked.

spans.text: In the view negative condition, participants attended to the content of negative pictures and responded naturally, allowing themselves to have whatever reaction the picture would normally evoke in them.
distract
In the distract condition, participants were asked to think about a neutral situation that was unrelated to the negative picture presented

description.value: Participants downregulated their emotional response to a negative picture by thinking about an unrelated neutral situation, such as preparing breakfast or going to the supermarket, without averting their gaze from the picture.

spans.text: In the distract condition, participants were asked to think about a neutral situation that was unrelated to the negative picture presented (e.g. preparing breakfast or going to the supermarket) without averting their gaze from the displayed scene
reappraise

In the reappraisal condition, they were instructed to reduce the intensity of their emotional response by reinterpreting the displayed negative situation to happen either in a pleasant context or with a pleasant ending

description.value: Participants downregulated their emotional response to a negative picture by reinterpreting the situation as occurring in a pleasant context or having a pleasant ending (positive reappraisal).

spans.text: In the reappraisal condition, they were instructed to reduce the intensity of their emotional response by reinterpreting the displayed negative situation to happen either in a pleasant context or with a pleasant ending [positive reappraisal, 15 , 46 ].

instructions.value: Participants viewed neutral or negative pictures and either responded naturally, distracted themselves by thinking about an unrelated neutral situation without averting their gaze, or reappraised the negative situation as occurring in a pleasant context or having a pleasant ending.
